units.translation: 222. ἐλάχηνεν: he dug, he excavated. It ends with the sense of "he prepared."
224. θυώδεϊ νᾶεν: water mixed with spices flowed, or fragrant oil.

225-27a. But she kept pouring forth water: Apollonius, saying that at the setting of the Pleiades the spring flows warm, and at their rising cold, did not present the season accurately. For there are two risings of the fixed stars and two settings. The morning rising is when a star first stands outside the rays of the sun and is seen rising before it; the morning setting is when, the sun being toward the east, a star is seen near the west setting last of all those that set during that night. The evening rising is when, at sunset, a star is seen in the east rising first of all those that rise during that night. The evening setting is said to occur when, at sunset, a star is seen setting before the others along with it, before it comes under the rays of the sun. The entire time under the rays is called concealment.
17 Autolycus, On Risings and Settings I Definitions; Geminus, Elements of Astronomy XIII 5, 14

The Pleiades, daughters of Pleione (daughter of Oceanus) and Atlas, as some say, received their name from their mother; or rather from the word πλειών, which means "year," for they are signs of winter and summer. They always travel in the opposite direction to Orion. For Orion is said to have met Pleione with her daughters in Boeotia, and falling in love with her he pursued her, while she fled. They say their flight was unceasing, and thus the Pleiades were placed among the stars, fleeing from Orion.
